input.message: Can you build me a full-body strength routine, no equipment, for twice a week?

output.reply:
Look, with travel and zero equipment, we keep it simple, honest, and high-quality. No skipping corners just because there are no dumbbells.

I built you a full-body routine called Full-Body Bodyweight Strength dosed for twice a week. Here is how we run it:

1. Warm-up & Activation: Single-leg glute bridges (10 reps each side, 2 sets) to fire up that right glute before anything else, plus bird dogs (8 reps each side).
2. Lower Body: Bodyweight Bulgarian split squats (3x8 each side with a slow 3s descent) and single-leg bodyweight RDLs (3x8 each side) for posterior chain.
3. Upper & Core: Push-ups (3x15 clean reps, chest to floor), doorframe rows (3x10 with a solid squeeze), and plank shoulder taps (3x10 each side) to hold the line.

Run this twice a week with at least 48 hours between them. Focus on the tempo and owning every rep. What day are you hitting the first one?

messages.text: Can you build me a full-body strength routine, no equipment, for twice a week?

paragraphs:
Look, with travel and zero equipment, we keep it simple, honest, and high-quality. No skipping corners just because there are no dumbbells.

I built you a full-body routine called Full-Body Bodyweight Strength dosed for twice a week. Here is how we run it:

1. Warm-up & Activation: Single-leg glute bridges (10 reps each side, 2 sets) to fire up that right glute before anything else, plus bird dogs (8 reps each side).
2. Lower Body: Bodyweight Bulgarian split squats (3x8 each side with a slow 3s descent) and single-leg bodyweight RDLs (3x8 each side) for posterior chain.
3. Upper & Core: Push-ups (3x15 clean reps, chest to floor), doorframe rows (3x10 with a solid squeeze), and plank shoulder taps (3x10 each side) to hold the line.

Run this twice a week with at least 48 hours between them. Focus on the tempo and owning every rep. What day are you hitting the first one?

messages.text: Two things - I want to permanently swap the core phase out of the full-body strength routine you just built me, going forward, my lower back doesn't handle it well, every time, not just today. And separately, can you restructure this week specifically - add a 20 minute mobility session on Saturday, just for this week.

paragraphs:
Look, if your lower back does not agree with the core work, forcing it is how you end up sidelined. We listen to the body every single time. I went ahead and permanently pulled the core phase out of the full_body_bodyweight_strength routine. 

For this week, I also added that 20-minute mobility session onto today's schedule for Saturday. Keep the movement gentle, breathe through the tight spots, and let me know how the back responds.

input.message: That's it for today, wrap this up.

output.reply: You got it, Sky. Plan is set, core phase is dropped from that template, and mobility is on the board for today. Get after the movement, protect that back, and rest up. Catch you tomorrow.
